SELF-PLAY
PRETRAINING
WITH ZERO DATA

Aditya Cowsik et al. · arXiv:2609.30063

THE EXPERIMENT

Can self-generated programs teach a model to predict unseen natural data?

01 Generator and learner begin with random weights.

02 Programs produce the learner’s byte-sequence training data.

03 Held-out natural datasets measure zero-shot transfer.

Cowsik et al. · §1–2 · arXiv:2609.30063

The training loop

A generator proposes programs; a universal machine runs them into bytes; the learner predicts the bytes. A reward updates the generator toward programs that extend the learner’s recent progress.

Cowsik et al. · Fig. 1, top · arXiv:2609.30063

GENERATOR OBJECTIVE

Reward learning progress, not raw difficulty

r(x) = |〈∇L(x; θnow), P ⊙ (θpast − θnow)〉|

Already mastered

Small learner gradient → little reward

Unlearnable noise

Gradient misaligned with recent learning → little reward

Current frontier

Substantial, aligned gradient → high reward

The paper uses an AdamW-preconditioned gradient-alignment score over a growing lookback window.

Cowsik et al. · §2.2, Eq. 2 · arXiv:2609.30063

Cowsik et al. · Table 1 and §3.1 · arXiv:2609.30063

Zero-shot loss falls with self-play compute

Compute-optimal frontiers on held-out text, CIFAR-10 images and melody show lower validation bits per byte as effective self-play compute increases. No natural-data gradient updates are used.

Cowsik et al. · Fig. 1, lower left · arXiv:2609.30063

Transfer beyond language-like data

On images, melody, audio and speech, the teal self-play curves fall more consistently than the fixed universal-program prior; the language-oriented PCFG baseline varies by domain.

Cowsik et al. · Fig. 2, upper row · arXiv:2609.30063

Text and code baselines

On text and code, the PCFG baseline is competitive or stronger; self-play still improves with compute. These curves show compute-optimal frontiers, including ensemble choices.

Cowsik et al. · Fig. 2, lower row · arXiv:2609.30063

Later generators make more useful data

A fresh 1M-parameter learner trained on corpora from later generator checkpoints finds more extractable structure and lower held-out text, audio and image loss.

Cowsik et al. · Fig. 3 · arXiv:2609.30063

In-context learning on six held-out tasks

With more demonstrations, the self-play learner improves on reverse string, stack, associative recall, sum, max and min. The fixed universal-prior and PCFG baselines transfer less broadly.

Cowsik et al. · Fig. 4 · arXiv:2609.30063

How the learner solves SUM in context

As examples accumulate, predictions shift from frequent bytes to copying, then partial arithmetic, then the correct SUM result; predictive entropy first rises and later falls.

Cowsik et al. · Fig. 5 · arXiv:2609.30063

Warm-starting natural-data pretraining

For a 24.4M-parameter learner, self-play initialization reaches each measured loss level with fewer natural-data tokens on DCLM text, CIFAR-10 images and ESC-50 audio.

Cowsik et al. · Fig. 6 · arXiv:2609.30063

EXPERIMENTAL BOUNDARY

What the results establish

Zero-data training

No natural data enters the learner or generator gradient updates.

Limited model scale

Experiments use models below 25M parameters and a 4,096-token context.

Model selection

DCLM and DNA validation loss guide hyperparameter selection, creating limited natural-data leakage.

Scope of transfer

The paper tests byte-level prediction and small-model warm starts; it does not establish large-model performance.
